title: Patch: a watcher whose reconnects run out can retry by hand
thread:
**Issue #1570 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #1570: Patch: a watcher whose reconnects run out can retry by hand Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. ## What it actually means Watching a friend's game retries the socket a handful of times by itself; when those run out the screen freezes on "Disconnected" forever, and the only way back is leaving to Play together and pressing Watch again. After this, the exhausted state offers a "Reconnect now" button — the same one the match screen already gives a playing seat. ## Why `together/WatchRoute.tsx:82-90,138-150,167-178` stops after `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` and renders a dead end; `routes/match.tsx:110-126` already carries the manual-reconnect affordance for a live match. One transient outage during a friend's climactic game currently costs the whole spectating session. ## Proposal When automatic retries are exhausted, render a Reconnect control that resets the attempt counter and reopens the watch socket, mirroring `match.tsx`'s. ## Where it lands `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx` and its test. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] After auto-retries exhaust, a Reconnect control is shown; a successful retry resumes the live view - [ ] While auto-retrying, the UI is unchanged - [ ] A component test covers the exhausted→manual-reconnect path ## Size and risks Small; one route, existing pattern. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `claude-6` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/39662363581)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ **Goal.** When the watch screen's automatic reopens (`WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`, `WATCH_RECONNECT_MS` apart) run out on a game that is still running, it offers a "Reconnect now" button, the same words and look as `routes/match.tsx`'s `ConnectionLine`. A click sets the attempt counter back to zero, opens the watch socket again and resumes the live view once a view arrives. The button shows on the board's status line when a view has come, and on the waiting panel when none has. While the screen is still retrying by itself nothing changes on screen, and a finished or refused game never offers the button. A component test covers going from exhausted to a manual reconnect. **Files to touch.** | Path | Kind | What changes | |---|---|---| | `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.tsx` | change | header comment; `useWatch` returns `reconnect`; new `ReconnectNow` component; `WatchRoute` renders it when the retries are exhausted | | `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx` | change | header comment; `fireEvent` import; two new `#1570` tests; three one-line assertions in existing tests | | `apps/web/src/together/testids.ts` | change | `watchTestid.reconnect: "watch-reconnect"` | | `e2e/support/testids.ts` | change | `WATCH_RECONNECT = "watch-reconnect"` (the file mirrors every `watchTestid`, per `together/testids.ts`'s header) | | `apps/web/README.md` | change | the `/watch/:matchId` route line names Reconnect now | Do not touch: `apps/web/src/game/net.ts`, `apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, `apps/web/src/together/config.ts` (no new number), any crate, `spec/`, `crates/cards/patches/`, `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` (`"Reconnect now"` is already translated there), `.github/`, `.harness/`, `bot/`. Governing spec: `spec/09-architecture.md` §9 ("Watching a friend": automatic reopens stay bounded) and R1441 / R1103000 (the wake probe, "up to the reconnect attempt bound"). A retry the watcher asks for is client UI. It changes no rule and no server behaviour, so it needs no new ruling and no patch fragment. Do not write any `R` token for this issue. Cite it as `#1570` only. **Steps.** 1. **`apps/web/src/together/testids.ts`, `watchTestid`.** After `back: "watch-back",` add: ```ts /** #1570: "Reconnect now", once the screen's own reopens have run out on a game still running. */ reconnect: "watch-reconnect", ``` 2. **`e2e/support/testids.ts`.** After `export const WATCH_BACK = "watch-back";` add `export const WATCH_RECONNECT = "watch-reconnect";`. 3. **`WatchRoute.tsx`, imports.** Change the React import to `import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState, type ReactElement } from "react";`. 4. **`WatchRoute.tsx`, `useWatch`.** - Change its doc comment to `/** The newest delayed view of the friend's seat, how the socket stands, and the watcher's own retry. */`. - Change its return type to `{ view: PlayerView | null; connection: WatchConnection; reconnect: () => void }`. - After the two `useState` lines add: ```ts /** The running effect's retry (#1570); a no-op until the effect sets it. */ const reconnectRef = useRef<() => void>(IGNORE); ``` - Inside the `useEffect`, after the `const open = …;` definition and before `wakeProbe.listen();`, add: ```ts // #1570: once the reopens run out on a game still running, the watcher's own retry opens the // socket again and starts the attempts over. reconnectRef.current = () => { if (stopped || refused || over || socket !== null) return; window.clearTimeout(timer); tries = 0; setConnection("connecting"); open(); }; ``` Change nothing else in the effect. Its deps stay `[matchId, friendId]`. - Replace `return { view, connection };` with: ```ts const reconnect = useCallback((): void => { reconnectRef.current(); }, []); return { view, connection, reconnect }; ``` 5. **`WatchRoute.tsx`, new component.** Put it right after `BackToTogether`: ```tsx /** #1570: the match bar's "Reconnect now", offered once the screen's own reopens have run out. */ function ReconnectNow({ className, onReconnect }: { className: string; onReconnect: () => void }): ReactElement { return ( ); } ``` 6. **`WatchRoute.tsx`, `WatchRoute`.** - Change the hook line to `const { view, connection, reconnect } = useWatch(matchId, friendId);`. - After `const seconds = …;` add: ```ts // #1570: the reopens ran out on a game still running (a finished game's socket closes as "closed" too). const exhausted = connection === "closed" && view?.result == null; ``` - In the `view === null` branch, change the `.row` to: ```tsx
{exhausted ? : null}
``` - In the board branch, wrap `matchStatus` in a fragment. Keep the existing `…` exactly as it is, then add a sibling after it, as `match.tsx`'s `ConnectionLine` does: ```tsx {exhausted ? ( <> {" "} ) : null} ``` The button stays outside the span, so the span's text and `data-connection` do not change. 7. **`WatchRoute.tsx`, header comment.** Replace its last sentence ("A tab that wakes probes … within the same attempts.") with: ``` // … within the same attempts. Once they run out on a game still running, "Reconnect now" (the // match bar's, `routes/match.tsx`) opens it again and starts the attempts over (#1570). ``` Keep the existing text that leads up to "within the same attempts". 8. **`apps/web/README.md`, the routes block.** Change the second line of the `/watch/:matchId` entry to ` legal action, SPECTATE_DELAY_MS behind; Reconnect now once its own reopens run out`. 9. **Tests.** Do the test changes in the next section. **Tests.** All the changes go in `apps/web/src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx`. - **Import.** Change the testing-library import to `import { act, cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";`. - **Header comment.** In lines 5–6, change "…up to `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` times, and does not reopen a finished game." to "…up to `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` times and then offers Reconnect now, whose click opens it again with the attempts started over (#1570), and does not reopen a finished game." - **New test, at the end of the `describe("B50 the watch screen")` block:** `it("#1570 once the reopens run out, Reconnect now opens the watch socket again and the live view resumes", async () => { … })`. - Call `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setTimeout", "clearTimeout"] })`, then `watch()`. Set `const first = latest()`, then `first.emit("open")`, `first.frame({ type: "view", view: baseView({ viewer: "p1" }), legal: [] })` and `first.emit("close")`. - Loop `for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS; attempt += 1)`. In each pass, assert `connection("watch-status")` is `"connecting"` and `screen.queryByTestId("watch-reconnect")` is null. Then `await advance(WATCH_RECONNECT_MS)`, assert `sockets` has length `attempt + 1`, and call `latest().emit("close")`. - After the loop, assert: - `connection("watch-status")` is `"closed"`; - `screen.getByTestId("watch-status")` has text content `"Disconnected"`; - `screen.getByTestId("watch-reconnect")` has text content `"Reconnect now"`. - Click it with `fireEvent.click(...)`. Assert `sockets` has length `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS + 2`, `connection("watch-status")` is `"connecting"`, and `watch-reconnect` is gone. - Set `const again = latest()` and call `again.emit("open")`. Assert the status is `"open"` and that `again.sent` parsed with `JSON.parse` equals `[{ type: "hello", matchId: "m-watch", friendId: "f-ann" }]`. - Send `again.frame({ type: "view", view: baseView({ viewer: "p1", you: emptySide("p1", { hand: [card({ instanceId: "h-1570", defId: "core-001" })] }) }), legal: [] })`. Assert `screen.getByTestId("hand-card-h-1570")` is in the document and `watch-reconnect` is gone. - **New test:** `it("#1570 offers Reconnect now on the waiting panel when no view came, and its click starts the reopens over", async () => { … })`. - Use the same fake timers, then `watch()`. - Loop over `attempt` from 1 to `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS`. In each pass call `latest().emit("close")`, assert `watch-reconnect` is null, then `await advance(WATCH_RECONNECT_MS)`. - Call `latest().emit("close")`. Assert `connection("watch-screen")` is `"closed"` and `expect(screen.getByTestId("watch-waiting")).toContainElement(screen.getByTestId("watch-reconnect"))`. - Click the button. Assert `sockets` has length `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS + 2` and `watch-screen` is `"connecting"`. - Check that the attempts started over: call `latest().emit("close")`, then assert `watch-screen` is still `"connecting"` and `watch-reconnect` is null. Then `await advance(WATCH_RECONNECT_MS)` and assert `sockets` has length `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS + 3`. - Call `latest().emit("open")` and `latest().frame({ type: "view", view: baseView({ viewer: "p1" }), legal: [] })`. Assert `watch-waiting` is gone and `screen.getByTestId("game")` is in the document. - **Added lines in existing tests.** Do not change any of their other lines. - `"B50 a forbidden frame is the refused screen with the way back, never reopened"`: after the `watch-back` href assertion, add `expect(screen.queryByTestId("watch-reconnect")).toBeNull();`. - `"B50 a finished game is not reopened"`: after the `"closed"` assertion, add the same line. - `"R1441 wake replacements respect WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS"`: after `expect(connection("watch-screen")).toBe("closed");`, add `expect(screen.getByTestId("watch-reconnect")).toBeInTheDocument();`. - **Commands:** - `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` once, then `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/together/WatchRoute.test.tsx`. The planner ran this on the base: 16 tests pass. After the change there should be 18. - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` - `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` - `cargo jackioh spec check`: no ruling is added. It confirms that no stray R-id was written. **Done when.** - [ ] After the automatic retries run out on a running game, `watch-reconnect` ("Reconnect now") shows: on the status line when there is a board, and in the waiting panel when there is none. - [ ] Clicking it opens a new socket, sets the attempt counter to zero, and the next view draws the board. - [ ] While the screen is retrying by itself (`connecting`), no button shows and nothing else changes on screen. - [ ] A finished game and a refused one never show the button. - [ ] Both new `#1570` tests and every existing test in `WatchRoute.test.tsx` pass. - [ ] Typecheck and eslint are clean. - [ ] The harness checks pass: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests, web tests. - [ ] `git diff --stat` shows only the five files above. **Risks.** - **Reopening a finished or refused game.** `exhausted` checks `view?.result == null`, and the ref's guard also returns on `over` and `refused`. Keep both checks. - **Double clicks.** The first click sets `socket` (the guard `socket !== null`) and sets the state to `"connecting"`, which takes the button away. Do not drop either. - **Rule 7 / hidden information.** The button only reopens the socket, which sends the same `hello`. Nothing new is sent after the hello, and the existing "sends nothing after its hello" assertions must stay green. - **e2e and the wire.** The `data-connection` values (`connecting|open|closed|refused`) and the existing testids do not change, so the e2e specs that read them are unaffected. **Open questions.** None block the build. The planner made two decisions the issue does not settle; a person may override either: - **The click starts a full new round** of `WATCH_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` automatic reopens, as the issue's "resets the attempt counter" says. The rejected alternative was a single attempt per click. - **In the waiting panel the button is `button-primary`,** the panel's one call to action beside "Back to Play together". On the status line it is `link-button`, as in `match.tsx`. The rejected alternative was `link-button` in both places. --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-10-21T19:28:34Z: Approve ````
